transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? I'm here to help you with whatever you're going through.

I came in because... well, I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake replaying client models in my head, over and over. And then I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach just tight in knots. I go to work feeling like I never actually rested. It's really taking a toll.
When you lie awake at night, is it mainly that you have trouble falling asleep initially, or do you fall asleep okay but then wake up later and can't get back to sleep?

It's honestly a bit of both, like I was just mentioning. At the start of the night, I have trouble falling asleep because my brain is just stuck on those client models. But then, even when I finally manage to drift off, I end up waking up again at 3 or 4 AM with that tight feeling in my stomach. Once I'm up at that hour, I can't get back to sleep at all. So I'm just not getting any real rest on either end of the night.
During the day, do you find yourself feeling unusually worried, tense, or on edge most of the time, even when there isn't a specific problem at hand?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I walk around feeling worried or on edge when there isn't a problem. If I'm stressed, it's usually about work, like those client accounts I mentioned. But just having a general, nervous feeling for no reason... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that.
During the day, do you find yourself feeling particularly fatigued or sleepy, even after trying to get some rest?

Well, I do feel really tired during the day, but it's not like I'm falling asleep at my desk or anything. I just feel... exhausted. Like I said, I'm not getting much sleep at night, so it makes sense that I'm dragging during the day. I wouldn't say I'm sleepy, just really drained.
Do you find yourself feeling irritable, moody, or easily frustrated during the day, especially because of how poorly you're sleeping?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely tired, but I don't think I'm taking it out on anyone. I'm not snapping at people or feeling unusually frustrated. I just kind of keep my head down and try to get through the day, honestly.
Have you noticed any days where you feel anxious or uneasy for no clear reason, even when things at work are going smoothly?

Um, no, not really. I think I mentioned it a minute ago, but I don't really get nervous or uneasy out of nowhere. If things at work are going smoothly, I'm not sitting there feeling anxious about it. I'm mostly just dealing with feeling so drained all the time, but... no, no random anxiety.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when it's not related to work stress?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's most days, honestly. I just move through the office, and even my apartment, with this heavy, gray feeling. It's like I'm just going through the motions. And sometimes, I'm just trying not to cry when someone asks me a completely normal question. It's just this constant sadness that doesn't really go away.
How often do you feel this sadness and like you're just going through the motions — is it every day, most days, or only occasionally?

It's... well, like I mentioned a second ago, it's most days. Honestly, it feels like almost every day at this point. I don't really have days where I wake up and feel completely normal or light. It's just always there.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, don't bring you the same pleasure anymore?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy seeing my friends, and I still like my hobbies. I mean, I might be really drained when I actually go do them, but the enjoyment itself is still there. So, no, I haven't really lost interest in those kinds of things.
Is the sadness you're feeling typically present most of the day, nearly every day, or does it come and go in a way that’s more tied to specific moments or stressors?

Like I mentioned earlier, it doesn't really come and go with stress. It's present most of the day. I just spend most days moving through the office, and even my apartment, with that heavy, gray feeling I talked about. I'm really just going through the motions the whole time, and it just stays with me... like I said, to the point where I'm trying not to cry when someone asks me a completely normal question. So, yeah, it's definitely there most of the day, not just tied to specific moments.
Has this feeling of sadness or heaviness been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Well, much longer than two weeks. It's... it's actually been going on for about three years now. It started ever since a merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division at work. So, yes, it's been nearly every day for years, not just weeks.
Have you noticed that you often lack energy or feel fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven't been doing anything particularly taxing?

No, I wouldn't say I feel fatigued or lack energy like that. I mean, I mentioned earlier that I feel drained sometimes when I go out to do things, but it's not a constant lack of energy or physical tiredness every day. It's really just that heavy feeling I described, rather than feeling physically exhausted for no reason.
Have you found yourself being overly hard on yourself, feeling like you're a failure, or feeling guilty about things more often than usual?

Yes, I definitely feel that way a lot. I guess... well, for example, if one of the managers at work questions one of my financial projections, even just a normal question, I immediately take it as confirmation that I'm just not as sharp as I used to be. I start feeling like everyone can see that I'm failing at my job. It's like I'm just waiting to be found out. So, yes, I am very hard on myself lately.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing on your work or thinking clearly lately?

Yes, definitely. Um, for example, spreadsheets that used to be second nature to me... they now take me hours to get through. I just keep losing the thread of what I'm doing. I end up rereading the same assumptions over and over again. And even after all that, I still worry I've missed something completely obvious right before a presentation. It's just really hard to keep my thoughts straight.
